one_line: Local-first reviewed action packs turn authenticated tabs into bounded agent tools.
what_it_does: Registers reviewed declarative action packs in a user session, with origin binding, drift protection, bounded output, and human approval for writes.
leverage_rationale: The intended experience depends on structured, typed tools sharing the user's authenticated browser state; screenshot/UI automation cannot comparably provide the same reviewed, fail-closed, bounded interface.
leverage_evidence: Frame sheets show action-pack registry/runtime framing and authenticated agent-operable site concept.
About describes exact-origin packs, reviewed fingerprints, declarative manifests, bounded untrusted output, and human-authorized writes.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent architecture and polished explanatory/demo surfaces, but no submitted video and limited end-to-end runtime proof cap execution confidence.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot shows a named demo with data-source and booking interfaces.
Frames show registry, pack inspection, and result-state concepts.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete operations problem: agents cannot safely operate the many authenticated sites where teams work, while preserving human authority.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets operations teams across monitoring, scheduling, payer portals, and admin dashboards.
About articulates safety and adoption barriers directly.
creativity_rationale: The inversion of adoption—users turning existing authenticated tabs into APIs via reviewed packs—is a memorable and ambitious interaction/model shift.
creativity_evidence: Frames explicitly present the 'login already sees everything' and reviewed action-pack registry concepts.
Architecture combines local runtime, provenance, bounded output, drift failure, and approval.
usability_note: Conceptual packaging is clear, though the packet does not show enough live interaction detail.
red_flags: No submitted video; frame sheets are largely presentation/storyboard evidence.
About text is truncated in the packet.
standouts: Strong safety model and adoption thesis.
WebMCP is central rather than decorative.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-leverage agent infrastructure with credible safety design; merits deeper verification.

one_line: A social-deduction match lets a human and an external agent play as separate players.
what_it_does: Runs a multi-phase bluffing, discussion, power, and voting game where an external WebMCP agent reads state and acts autonomously.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools allow the agent to observe changing game state, communicate, use powers, vote, and persist across rounds; generic UI driving is materially less reliable for this interactive loop.
leverage_evidence: About specifies seven tools for state, discussion, powers, messaging, voting, and continuation across rounds.
Pitch defines human and agent as independent players in one live match.
execution_rationale: The concept and claimed flow are coherent, but no frame sheets or video were submitted, so end-to-end completion is not demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Devpost text describes three game phases and an external agent role.
Live demo is reported alive in the packet.
impact_rationale: It offers a clear entertainment and demonstration use case for agents that must reason, communicate, and react socially in a changing environment.
impact_evidence: About identifies humans trying to identify hidden AI players and agents trying to blend in.
The game exercises contextual agent behavior beyond form filling.
creativity_rationale: Using WebMCP for an agent as a socially deceptive player is a fresh, memorable application of the medium.
creativity_evidence: Social-deduction framing makes the agent's reasoning and communication part of gameplay.
Submission explicitly contrasts this with ordinary SaaS automation demos.
usability_note: The phase model sounds approachable, but visual proof is absent.
red_flags: No frame sheets or submitted video.
Core behavior is primarily asserted in text.
standouts: Agent is a first-class player, not a UI macro.
Good use of changing shared state.
advance_reason: Strong creative WebMCP use and plausible live demo, despite thin evidence.

one_line: Evidence reconciliation stages closeout decisions while keeping human approval separate from application.
what_it_does: Audits synthetic construction closeout requirements, maps evidence to blockers, stages a tokenized approval, and applies only after explicit human confirmation.
leverage_rationale: Shared structured state, staged writes, one-time approval tokens, and deterministic read/write boundaries make agent-human closeout review substantially safer and more precise than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: About specifies seven read and three write native Site Tools.
Instructions describe read state, blocker identification, stage-without-mutation, apply token, consumed-token retry, and reset.
execution_rationale: The central 9/14 to 10/14 workflow, approval boundary, and consumed-token behavior are unusually complete and visually evidenced, though only claimed rather than observed live.
execution_evidence: Frames show fire-damper evidence mapping, no-status-mutation staging, and separate human approval.
About gives a reproducible end-to-end judge flow with named tools and expected states.
impact_rationale: Construction handoff has a specific, costly evidence problem, and this product directly addresses stale, missing, mislinked, and scope-ambiguous proof.
impact_evidence: Audience includes general contractors, owner representatives, closeout coordinators, and commissioning teams.
Frames show criterion-level evidence, blockers, and decision lanes.
creativity_rationale: The separation of evidence reconciliation, scope lanes, approval, and application is a thoughtful interaction model for agent-assisted operational decisions.
creativity_evidence: Frames visibly distinguish proof mapping, staging without mutation, and human approval.
About emphasizes audit-ready handoff rather than generic checklist completion.
usability_note: The criterion/evidence/status layout and explicit approval controls appear understandable.
red_flags: No submitted video; frame evidence is a storyboard/contact sheet.
standouts: Excellent human-authority boundary.
Concrete reproducible state transitions and token replay handling.
advance_reason: High-value, well-scoped workflow with strong WebMCP leverage and unusually specific evidence.

one_line: Buyer and seller agents negotiate multi-dimensional deals while the human confirms the order.
what_it_does: Provides a multi-vendor storefront whose WebMCP tools support search, cart, coupons, add-ons, and multi-round buyer/seller negotiation before confirmation.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables two page-local agents to negotiate over price, quantity, freebies, shipping, and coupons against live shared state, a workflow not comparably replicated by generic clicking.
leverage_evidence: About describes buyer and store agents negotiating over several rounds through page tools.
Frames show storefront, catalog/loading states, and shopping-agent presentation.
execution_rationale: The architecture claims a single mutation path and explicit economic constraints, while visuals show a coherent storefront/catalog; negotiation completion is not directly visible.
execution_evidence: About specifies OffersService.applyTurn as the sole negotiation transition and buyer/seller hard limits.
Frames show polished storefront and catalog states.
impact_rationale: Shoppers have a clear desire to delegate tedious price and deal optimization while retaining final purchase authority.
impact_evidence: Pitch names concrete deal dimensions and human confirmation.
About reports a broad 95k+ product catalog and no-payment-without-confirmation boundary.
creativity_rationale: Agent-to-agent haggling over a bundle of deal dimensions is a novel, memorable commerce interaction with meaningful ambition.
creativity_evidence: Multi-round buyer/store agent negotiation is central to the concept.
Human confirmation is integrated as the final interaction boundary.
usability_note: Storefront/catalog presentation appears polished; negotiation UX is not shown directly.
red_flags: Frame sheets show browsing/loading more clearly than a settled negotiation.
Some evidence is descriptive rather than directly observed.
standouts: Strong agent-to-agent interaction model.
Explicit economic invariants and human purchase confirmation.
advance_reason: One of the strongest leverage/creativity concepts, with credible implementation detail.

one_line: An agent-directed studio writes, stages, reviews, and exports fictional coding-agent sessions.
what_it_does: Lets an agent author scripts, control camera/theme/timing, render SVG/video, inspect frames, propose patches, and wait for human approval.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates on deterministic stage state and receives facts such as timeline and frame inspection that are difficult to obtain reliably by clicking; it directly authors and revises the artifact.
leverage_evidence: Transcript documents tool discovery, script writing, camera, choice edits, voice input, frame inspection, and export.
About lists 13 site tools including load_script, inspect_timeline, snapshot_frame, fit_duration, propose_patch, approve_proposal, and export.
execution_rationale: The submitted 170-second video transcript and frame sheets cover a complete authoring-to-render-to-export workflow with approvals, alternate surfaces, and deterministic output.
execution_evidence: Video exists and transcript describes studio, agent rail, staged script, revisions, rendering, and export.
Frames show repeated studio/stage states and product UI.
impact_rationale: README/doc authors, speakers, and creators have a real need for reproducible, secret-free, reshootable coding-session visuals.
impact_evidence: About names READMEs, docs, talks, and posts as target uses.
Privacy and deterministic rendering address real recording limitations.
creativity_rationale: The concept of an agent directing a fictional session as a renderable stage, with inspectable frames and human-approved rewrites, is highly original and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Transcript shows choices, voice input, theme/camera changes, terminal/app surfaces, and export.
About emphasizes agent working on the stage itself, not a guessed representation.
usability_note: The stage plus agent rail and approval cards form a clear creative workflow.
standouts: End-to-end video evidence.
Strong artifact inspection and approval model.
advance_reason: Exceptional demonstrated execution paired with transformative creative use of WebMCP.

one_line: A cooking copilot turns pantry contents into an approved shopping plan and guided dinner.
what_it_does: Plans diet/time-aware meals, identifies missing groceries, waits for human approval, then guides cooking with substitutions, trace, and timers.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools coordinate planning, pantry state, approval boundaries, and guided execution; a general agent could approximate it but with meaningful state and safety friction.
leverage_evidence: About describes visible agent actions, Agent Trace, human-approved missing groceries, and no purchase/payment tool.
Frames show planner, approval, guided cooking, timer, and completion states.
execution_rationale: The frame set covers a coherent planner-to-approval-to-guided-cooking-to-ready flow with responsive finish states.
execution_evidence: Five gallery/frames visibly represent planner, shopping approval, guided cooking, timer, and completion.
About names persistent timer and substitutions.
impact_rationale: Meal planning is a concrete recurring problem involving pantry constraints, diet, time, shopping, and next-step guidance.
impact_evidence: Pitch and about identify the chain of decisions that blocks dinner.
Visible workflow ends with a ready confirmation and guided steps.
creativity_rationale: It is a fresh, well-integrated cooking-copilot synthesis with agent trace and explicit purchasing boundaries, though the category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Combines pantry-aware planning, substitutions, human shopping approval, and cooking guidance.
Frames show the full multi-stage experience.
usability_note: Planner and guided mode appear accessible, with persistent trace and timer.
red_flags: No submitted video; visual evidence is still-frame based.
standouts: Clear safety boundary around shopping/payment.
Strong end-to-end everyday workflow.
advance_reason: Complete and useful workflow with credible agent-human boundaries.

one_line: A deterministic CRM audit lets agents and humans co-review the same prioritized evidence.
what_it_does: Computes health scores and issue queues from synthetic CRM data, exposing bounded read-only tools that focus the corresponding human report row.
leverage_rationale: Structured deterministic summaries and synchronized row focus improve precision and shared state, though a general agent could obtain much of the same read-only result with friction.
leverage_evidence: About names three read-only tools and automatic focusing/highlighting of the same record.
Frames show CRM report/evidence review surfaces.
execution_rationale: The product scope is coherent and deterministic, but the packet has no gallery images and no video; end-to-end synchronization is claimed rather than shown.
execution_evidence: About specifies health score, category scores, prioritized queue, record evidence, and guidance.
Packet reports a live demo and public repo.
impact_rationale: CRM administrators and RevOps teams face real data-quality issues that undermine routing, reporting, automation, and agent behavior.
impact_evidence: About identifies missing ownership, stale deals, weak activity, and malformed fields.
Audience is specific and aligned.
creativity_rationale: Deterministic CRM health auditing with human-agent co-review is a useful new angle on a known diagnostic category, but not radically novel.
creativity_evidence: Read-only agent co-review and synchronized record focus are the distinct interaction.
Deterministic rules avoid asking an LLM to guess findings.
usability_note: Prioritized queues and focused records should be usable, but visual evidence is thin.
red_flags: Zero gallery images and no video.
Core co-review behavior is not visually demonstrated.
standouts: Deterministic findings and bounded read-only surface.
Good synchronization concept.
advance_reason: Credible practical tool, but Stage 2 should verify the live synchronization and tool surface.

one_line: A WebMCP agent controls a remote physical computer through TinyPilot without software on the target.
what_it_does: Exposes console observation, keyboard/mouse, diagnostics, networking, security, updates, and power operations as browser-native tools.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides precise structured control of a remote physical display/input channel, enabling agent operation of locked-down or legacy machines where ordinary browser automation cannot work.
leverage_evidence: About explains monitor/keyboard/mouse-only target compatibility and 75 tools.
Pitch and description cover physical appliance, shared display, and agent intervention.
execution_rationale: The claimed surface is broad and the physical integration is coherent, but this packet lacks video and gallery images, limiting observed completeness.
execution_evidence: About describes normal dashboard registration and isolated simulated desktop demo.
Packet reports live demo and public repo.
impact_rationale: Remote operation of installers, recovery consoles, locked-down devices, and legacy systems is a concrete high-value use case for organizations and support teams.
impact_evidence: About lists operating-system installers, recovery consoles, locked-down devices, and legacy systems.
Human can watch and intervene at any time.
creativity_rationale: Applying page-native agent tools to a physical KVM/remote-computer boundary is an ambitious and memorable extension beyond web-only automation.
creativity_evidence: Agent controls a physical computer via video and USB with no target-side agent software.
75-tool coverage spans operational device management.
usability_note: The shared console model is understandable, but live evidence is absent in this packet.
red_flags: No submitted video or frame sheets despite claims of physical demo video.
Hosted demo is simulated rather than physical hardware.
standouts: High practical impact and strong WebMCP necessity.
No software installation on controlled machine.
advance_reason: Potentially transformative infrastructure integration; verify physical/live behavior in Stage 2.

one_line: A research observatory traces commercial infrastructure behind information operations with agent and human provenance control.
what_it_does: Lets researchers and agents search, follow relationships, inspect cited evidence, retain leads, and assemble briefs across a source ecology.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP supplies a shared inspectable research terrain where agents can search, organize, and follow graph relationships while humans retain provenance and uncertainty decisions; generic UI automation would be materially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly says agents trace infrastructure, inspect evidence, and retain leads.
About describes live feed, notebook, Atlas Relay map, evidence demo, and purpose-built tools.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a broad thesis proof-of-concept with multiple research surfaces, but no video and no fully demonstrated end-to-end investigation.
execution_evidence: Seven gallery images/frame sheets show observatory, map, notebook, and research-output concepts.
About states the project is a proof of concept for a thesis.
impact_rationale: Researchers and journalists have a real need to connect scattered infrastructure, registry, platform, and reporting evidence without premature conclusions.
impact_evidence: About identifies scattered datasets and the need to preserve provenance, uncertainty, and interpretation.
Specific audience and research method are clearly articulated.
creativity_rationale: The focus on hidden commercial infrastructure and a six-level source ecology creates an original research interaction model pursued with ambitious observatory, map, notebook, and brief surfaces.
creativity_evidence: Thesis-driven framing goes beyond a chatbot beside a dashboard.
Frames and about describe Atlas Relay, live feed, notebook, and evidence graph concepts.
usability_note: Multiple research surfaces are promising, though breadth may increase complexity and the packet lacks live video.
red_flags: Proof-of-concept scope and no submitted video.
About text is truncated in the packet.
standouts: Distinctive thesis/research-method integration.
Strong provenance and uncertainty orientation.
advance_reason: High creativity and credible research value; merits deeper inspection of the actual evidence graph and agent flow.

one_line: A privacy-preserving browser audio suite lets an agent run multi-tool DSP workflows locally.
what_it_does: Offers 49 in-browser audio tools and WebMCP operations for trimming, silence removal, normalization, conversion, mastering, preview, and export without uploads.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives an agent structured control over local audio DSP and cross-tool handoff without uploading confidential audio; UI clicking cannot comparably provide precise, repeatable pipelines and numeric results.
leverage_evidence: About describes list_tools/open_tool routing, set_trim, send_to_tool, silence removal, loudness targeting, preview, and export.
Pitch emphasizes local audio never leaving the tab and one-sentence agent workflows.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a broad integrated suite and frames show tool catalog, waveform/editor states, and workflows, though no video is submitted.
execution_evidence: 49 tools are described as browser-local with no upload/account.
Frame sheets visibly show audio-tool interfaces and waveform/control states.
impact_rationale: Private voice notes, unreleased tracks, and confidential interviews have a real need for local audio processing, and the workflow reduces technical friction.
impact_evidence: About identifies privacy-sensitive audiences and the agent audio blind spot.
Concrete podcast-ready pipeline is described end to end.
creativity_rationale: Making local browser DSP legible and orchestrable by an agent, with cross-tool handoff and privacy as a feature, is a strong original application.
creativity_evidence: Agent routes itself through a catalog and chains four tools from one request.
No-upload constraint is integrated into the interaction model.
usability_note: One-file selection followed by visible waveform operations and export is a clear workflow.
red_flags: The underlying 49-tool suite appears pre-existing; only WebMCP integration may be new.
standouts: Very strong privacy and local-processing story.
Cross-tool agent pipeline is concrete and technically meaningful.
advance_reason: Excellent leverage and impact with a concrete, privacy-preserving end-to-end workflow; verify integration depth and origin in Stage 2.
